title: Western Blotting using the Bolt system
author: Doug Campbell
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jwqcpdw

steps.title: Prepare SDS-PAGE Samples
steps.instruction: Prepare samples for loading and the standard curve according to SOP #14.

steps.title: Prepare Electrophoresis Rig
steps.instruction: Set up the electrophoresis rig and prepare the running buffer.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 440 mL (per gel) of Bolt 1X running buffer according to the Bolt protocol quick sheet.
Set up the rig with metal prods from the electrophoresis clamps facing towards the middle and ensure the lid fits.
Pour running buffer into the rig until it is 1 cm above the metal conducting plate.

steps.title: Install Gel
steps.instruction: Carefully place the commercial gel into the rig using gloves.

substeps.instruction: Open the commercial gel package, rinse the wells, and discard the comb and sticker.
Place the gel in the rig and snap shut the clamp.
Discard gloves in the special waste container for acrylamide.

steps.title: Load Samples and Ladder
steps.instruction: Load heated, spun, and chilled samples and the molecular weight ladder into the gel.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the ladder by mixing 0.5 uL MagicMark and 4.5 uL NovexSharp (Life Tech).
Load samples and the ladder into the gel, using asymmetrical ladder loading to assist with orientation during imaging.

steps.title: Run SDS-PAGE
steps.instruction: Run the gels at 200 V for 22-35 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Use 1X MOPS buffer for proteins >70 kDA or 1X MES buffer for all other proteins.
Monitor the NovexSharp pre-stained ladder and run until the size range for the protein of interest is halfway down the gel.

steps.title: Prepare Transfer Materials
steps.instruction: Gather and prepare all necessary components for the transfer process.

substeps.instruction: Prepare ~200 mL of 1X transfer buffer (per blot) according to the Bolt protocol quick sheet.
Prepare a sheet of pre-cut PVDF with a notched corner (or nitrocellulose membrane).
Prepare 50 mL of methanol for PVDF rehydration.
Gather 2 sponges, 2 pre-cut filter papers, a blot module cassette, blot tweezers, a roller, a metal tool for plastic cracking, one small plastic dish, and one medium size plastic dish.

steps.title: Set Up Transfer Station
steps.instruction: Organize the workspace and prepare the transfer module.

substeps.instruction: Place instruments on a cookie sheet, methanol in the small plastic dish, and transfer buffer in the medium plastic container.
Pour a small amount of 1X transfer buffer onto the negatively charged module piece.
Soak and massage the first sponge, then place it in the pre-wetted module piece, ensuring all air bubbles are expelled (use the roller if needed).
Position sponges so the longer edge is along the bottom.
Soak and massage the top sponges and leave them in the buffer for later use.
For PVDF: Activate in methanol for at least 30 seconds, then place in the transfer bucket with filter paper on top to keep it submerged and prevent drying.
For nitrocellulose: Skip the methanol activation step.

steps.title: Extract Gel from Plates
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the gel from the pre-cast plates while wearing safety glasses.

substeps.instruction: Jam the metal tool between the two plates of the pre-cast gel (shorter plate upwards) and twist to open.
Remove the shorter plate and set it aside.
Cut off the wells and place them on the discarded plate.

steps.title: Assemble Transfer Sandwich
steps.instruction: Construct the transfer sandwich on the cookie sheet.

substeps.instruction: Place the first filter paper along the well line.
Flip the gel and push it off the plate using the metal tool through the sticker location.
Place the gel on the cookie sheet and cut off the foot (Lane #1 will be on the far right).
Gently place the PVDF on the gel with the notched side in the upper right corner and remove air bubbles.
Place a second piece of filter paper on top and gently roll the sandwich with the plastic roller.

steps.title: Execute Transfer
steps.instruction: Transfer proteins from the gel to the membrane.

substeps.instruction: Lift the sandwich and place it in the same orientation into the transfer module on the sponge.
Add the second sponge and close the module.
Place the module in the rig with feet facing the operator.
Fill the inner chamber of the cassette(s) with 1X transfer buffer (1 cm above electrode) and the outer space with cold tap water.
Fit the lid and transfer for 60 minutes at 30V (voltage may be optimized to 20V depending on protein size).

steps.title: Block Membranes
steps.instruction: Block the membranes to prevent non-specific binding.

substeps.instruction: Prepare blocking solution (5% fat-free milk powder or 2% ECL blocking solution) dissolved in 1X TBS-T (0.1%), NOT water.
Use 10 mL of solution for 1-hour room temperature incubation or 20 mL for overnight incubation in the fridge to account for evaporation.
Open modules and place the PVDF protein side up (the side that touched the gel) directly into the blocking solution, ensuring it does not dry out.

steps.title: Clean Up
steps.instruction: Dispose of materials and clean equipment.

substeps.instruction: Place the actual gel in the acrylamide waste bucket.
Discard used filter paper in the green garbage.
Rinse sponges multiple times in dH2O and press to expel water without bending or crushing them.
Rinse rigs in dH2O.
